name: Ammonite_2023_KQ14
source: Chen, Y.-T. et al. (2025), Nature Astronomy, doi:10.1038/s41550-025-02595-7, ''Discovery and dynamics of a Sedna-like object with a perihelion of 66 au''; elements as tabulated on Wikipedia (2023 KQ14), sourced from JPL Small-Body Database / MPC solution
selection_notes: Real object (discovered 2023, published 2025), NOT part of the original de la Fuente Marcos (2014) 13-object sample used for the rest of this catalog. Two known inconsistencies vs. the other 13 rows, kept explicit rather than silently normalized: (1) frame is BARYCENTRIC as tabulated by the source, not heliocentric like the other 13; (2) epoch is 2025-05-05, not the shared 2014-05-23 epoch of the other 13. Both offsets are small relative to a=251.9 AU but have not been rigorously propagated to a common heliocentric epoch here (WHFast in this pipeline treats osculating elements as-is, ignoring the epoch string — see docs/LIMITACOES.md). Included because it is the most consequential recent ETNO for the P9 anti-alignment claim: q=65.9 AU, longitude of perihelion far from the cluster (varpi = omega+Omega = 270.84 deg), which the discovery paper''s authors (Huang et al.) explicitly cite as evidence against simple P9 shepherding. Re-derive from a live JPL Horizons/SBDB pull at a common epoch before using this row for a quantitative (not just qualitative/robustness) claim.

name: 2017_OF201
source: Cheng, S., Li, J. & Yang, E. (2025), arXiv:2505.15806, Discovery of a dwarf planet candidate in an extremely wide orbit: 2017 OF201
selection_notes: Barycentric elements, epoch 2025-05-05, differs from the heliocentric/epoch-2014-05-23 standard of the original 13 objects (De la Fuente Marcos 2014) — same caveat as Ammonite_2023_KQ14, not propagated to a common epoch before use. q (perihelion) = 44.91 AU, derived from a and e. This object directly challenges the P9 alignment hypothesis (varpi = omega + Omega mod 360 = 306.9 deg, far outside the classical clustering near varpi ~ 60 deg per the discovery paper, Section 4.3).

name: Leleakuhonua_2015_TG387
source: Sheppard, S. S., Trujillo, C. A., Tholen, D. J. (2019), AJ 157, 139, A New High Perihelion Trans-Plutonian Inner Oort Cloud Object: 2015 TG387
selection_notes: Barycentric elements, epoch 2023-02-25, differs from the heliocentric/epoch-2014-05-23 standard of the original 13 objects — same caveat as Ammonite_2023_KQ14 and 2017_OF201, not propagated to a common epoch before use. q (perihelion) = 64.7 AU. The discovery paper simulates P9 shepherding and finds stable behavior similar to already-aligned ETNOs — this object is consistent with the clustering, unlike Ammonite and 2017 OF201.
